values.applies_where: Nearest point on the boundary of the other administration's country (Art. 4 §4.2.2 a)
values.table: Annex 4, Chapter 1, introductory text to Tables 4.1-4.4
values.notes: GE84 has NO trigger field strength. Coordination is triggered by DISTANCE: an administration is affected if the station is closer to its border than the coordination distance in Tables 4.1 (land), 4.2 (cold sea), 4.3 (warm sea), 4.4 (super-refractive) for the station's e.r.p. (dBW) and effective antenna height, linear interpolation, mixed path D_M = sum(d_i/d_T * D_i). The distances were computed from a 54 dB(uV/m) nuisance field with mean protection ratios 39 dB (tropospheric) and 47 dB (steady), taking the larger distance. Confirmed identical in the 1984 scan (scan PDF p. 61).

Use the distance tables, not these numbers, to reproduce the GE84 test.

ge84_coordination_distances_note: Tables 4.1-4.4 (printed pp. 55-58, PDF pp. 61-64) give coordination distances in km by e.r.p. 0-55 dBW (5 dB steps) and effective antenna height 10/37.5/75/150/300/600/1200/1800 m; not transcribed here (the task asked for field strengths). Example Table 4.1 land, 30 dBW: 250/250/260/270/290/320/360/400 km. Table 4.4 (super-refractive) is height-independent, 560 km at 0 dBW to 1480 km at 55 dBW.

method_notes.GE06: Single trigger value per band and system, applied through a coordination contour. Annex 4 Section I (Limits and methodology for determining when agreement with another administration is required; printed pp. 285-302, PDF pp. 293-310). NOTE: the trigger tables are in Section I and its Appendix 1, not Section II (Section II, printed p. 304, is 'Examination of conformity with the digital Plan entry'). For a modification to the Plan, take Table A.1.1 by the system modifying the Plan (DVB-T: 17/21/23/25 dB(uV/m) in Band III/IV/V-low/V-high), compute field strength with the Annex 2 Chapter 2 propagation model for 1% time, 50% locations, 10 m Rx height, notified e.r.p. and effective height; on 1 deg radials start at 1 000 km and step inward 10 km until the trigger is reached; an administration whose national boundary is intersected by or enclosed in the contour is affected. SFN: reference point at the centre of gravity of the transmitters, power sum. Allotment: reference network from each boundary test point (Appendix 3, +3 dB power margin for DVB-T RN). Contour capped at 1 000 km. Triggers are derived as Ftrigger = Fmed + fcorr - PR - CF (Appendix 2, eq. A.2.1), tropospheric PR, no receiving antenna discrimination, fcorr = 20 log10(f/fr) for fixed reception, 30 log10(f/fr) for portable/mobile, fr = 200 MHz (Band III) or 650 MHz (Bands IV/V). Definition (Annex 2, Chapter 1, §1.3.10, printed p. 74, PDF p. 82): 'Field-strength level which, when exceeded, determines that coordination is required'.
method_notes.GE84: No single trigger field strength. Article 4 §4.2.2 a) (printed p. 4, PDF p. 10): sound broadcasting of another administration is likely to be affected if the distance from the station to the nearest point of that country's boundary is less than the limit in Annex 4 Chapter 1, i.e. coordination distance Tables 4.1-4.4 by e.r.p. and effective antenna height and path type (land / cold sea / warm sea / super-refractive; mixed paths by weighted sum). Those distances were derived from a 54 dB(uV/m) nuisance field with mean protection ratios 39 dB tropospheric and 47 dB steady. §4.2.4 exempts power reductions, cases beyond the distances, and site moves <= 15 km (>= 1 kW) or <= 5 km (< 1 kW). Once identified, the consulted administration assesses by calculation (§4.3.7.1): usable field strength by the simplified multiplication method (Annex 2 Ch. 4, nuisance fields Esi = Pi + Eni(50,T) + Ai + Bi, sigma = 8.3 dB) at the transmitter site or specific service-area points; acceptable if <= 54 dB(uV/m) or increased by <= 0.5 dB over the reference usable field strength. Nuisance field: steady Es = P + E(50,50) + As, tropospheric Et = P + E(50,T) + At, use the larger (Annex 2 §3.5). Planning minimum usable field strength: 54 stereo / 48 mono dB(uV/m), rural, 10 m (Annex 2 §3.6).
method_notes.for_the_tool: For GE06 a fixed per-band trigger can be compared with a P.1546-type field strength at the Finnish border (1% time, 50% loc, 10 m). For GE84 the faithful test is the distance table, not a field-strength threshold; an implied border field strength (15 dB(uV/m) at 1% time / 7 dB(uV/m) at 50% time) is a derivation and must be labelled so.

not_found_or_uncertain: GE84 landing page https://www.itu.int/pub/R-ACT-RRC.6-1984 says 'not available'; the text used is the ITU dms_pub file R-ACT-RRC.5-1984 (title confirmed in PDF metadata and title page) plus the ITU History scan.

GE06 Table A.1.1 carries no bandwidth footnote, while A.1.9/A.1.10/A.2.x say the values relate to the 7 or 8 MHz bandwidth of the protected system; we assume A.1.1 is the same basis.
Location correction factor CF values used in Appendix 2 are not printed in Tables A.2.1/A.2.2 (they are in Annex 2 Chapter 3, not read).
